doc.title: Josephine Davies interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, October 14, 2025

title: Scores, piano parts and pen-and-paper versus Sibelius
summary: She writes loose 'ish' sketches and detailed piano voicings, starting on paper and then using Sibelius.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Well said again. A little shift here. In watching your videos, especially the live ones, I saw music stands some of the time with your drummer and bass player, and I really wanted to see what your scores look like. Do you – how much do you write out, and do you use non- – what I’ll describe as creative notation other than notes?

Ooo. Yeah. Probably. I do write things down most of the time. Sometimes that will be a scribble on a piece of paper and it will sort of say, I use the word “ish” quite a lot. So the B minor-ish, as in eh, we might have a sort of tonic area of B and let me see what happens. And I play with people who are so able to interpret anything. But it goes in its own direction no matter how much or how little I write. And then some of the more involved pieces will probably be a more traditional score where everyone has a sense of
what they’re doing. But I hope, even within those things there’s enough space for us to get away from the page and do our own thing and then come back to it. Yeah.
Do you hate writing piano parts if they’re anything more than chords?
No, no I love it. In fact I write --

Yeah, I love it. I write quite a lot of them, piano parts, stuff that I compose at the piano. And sometimes if I can be really specific about what I want because that’s how I’ve written it. So I rather than write the chord sequence I’ll actually write the voicing that I want or the pattern that I want the piano player to play. And that can be really specific. Yeah.
And are you still a pen and paper person? Pencil and paper or are you in Finale etcetera?

Pen and paper to start and then I will put it on Sibelius, for people to read, which actually I quite enjoy. I like making it all neat and then it’s there in case I want to do any edits the next time. And I have a friend who is only pen and paper and it’s always a challenge because his naturals look like sharps. I told him.
That’s a great way to slow down a recording session.
Is that a sharp or is that a natural?
